Q: Why Aren't `std::uniform_int_distribution<uint8_t>` and `std::uniform_int_distribution<int8_t>` Allowed? A:

Since C++26 (see P4037R1: Supporting signed char and unsigned char in random number generation), the restriction on uniform_int_distribution<uint8_t> (and 8-bit types) has been lifted. It has always been completely arbitrary because instead of outputting a random uint8_t in range, say, [0, 100], you can just output a random int in range [0, 100] and cast the result from int to uint8_t. In principle, any integer type could be supported as the result of a distribution without a problem. The new restriction is [rand.req.genl] p1.6:

If a template argument corresponding to a template parameter named IntType is neither a standard signed nor a standard unsigned integer type ([basic.fundamental]), nor an extended integer type whose width is greater or equal to that of char and less than or equal to that of long long, nor a member of an implementation-defined subset of integer types, the program is ill-formed.

uint8_t is allowed because it is either unsigned char (and thus a standard unsigned integer type) or an extended integer type with the same width as unsigned char.

Note that the "implementation-defined subset" part is there to allow things like uniform_int_distribution<__int128> or uniform_int_distribution<unsigned _BitInt(1)>, but only if the implementation wants to support such types and considers them to be extended integer types. Also note that some standard libraries have supported 8-bit integers in this context for a long time already, namely libc++ and libstdc++. See the paper for more details.

For generators (not for distributions), the restriction is not arbitrary; see the other answer in this thread. Some people are even of the opinion that supporting short in generators was a mistake.

Q: Getting sql query results in Codeignitor and display on web page A:

Good answer by Shafeeque TP, even better is to use the query builder or active record class provided by codeigniter. To do that, go to your application/config/autoload.php, go to $autoload['libraries'] and add 'database' to the array, that way you don't have to manually load it.

For the query part, simply do this:

$this->db->select('Channel', 'Which Company', 'Offer', 'Business Sector', 'url Link', 'Discount Code', 'Contact', 'Sector')
         ->from('form_deal_form')
         ->where(1)
         ->get()
         ->result();

Not sure the WHERE part of your query is correct, I just put a 1 for the sake of converting your query to the active record class. As a side note you don't have to use result(); to generate your query results, that was just an example. You can find more ways to generate results in the links provided by Shafeeque TP.

Q: Encoding issue when getting Database entries in Laravel 5 A:

Since the hex is C3A3 E2809A C2B9 C3A3 C692 ..., you have "double encoding". That is usually caused by...

  • The client had characters encoded as utf8 (good); and
  • SET NAMES latin1 lied by claiming that the client had latin1 encoding; and
  • The column in the table declared CHARACTER SET utf8 (good).

Had you also done utf8_encode() at that time?

Here's what happened. For the first character, you had E382B9. But, by saying latin1, that was treated as E3 82 B9, which in latin1 is ã‚¹. Those three characters we sent to the table, converting on the fly to utf8, as indicated on the table/column definition: C3A3 E2809A C2B9 -- the utf8 hex for those 3 characters.

Normaly, "double encoding" 'repairs' itself upon reading. That is the steps are reversed with two translations from utf8 to latin1 and you get back ス.

But apparently one of the translations was skipped.

mysql> SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'char%';
+--------------------------+--------------
| Variable_name            | Value
+--------------------------+--------------
| character_set_client     | utf8          **
| character_set_connection | utf8          **
| character_set_database   | latin1
| character_set_filesystem | binary
| character_set_results    | utf8          **
| character_set_server     | utf8mb4
| character_set_system     | utf8
| character_sets_dir       | ...
+--------------------------+------------

The three ** are set simultaneously when doing SET NAMES utf8. But I think you had some mixture, possibly

| character_set_client     | latin1
| character_set_connection | latin1
| character_set_results    | utf8

Not good.

If you need to recover the data, there is code in my lengthy charset blog.

I'm sorry; I don't know what it takes for Laravel to establish all three settings correctly. Perhaps you could get it to execute SET NAMES utf8 shortly after connecting.
